card.title: Symbol of Office
card.instruction: Choose one symbol, privilege, or position and treat control of it as proof of legitimate authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have the meeting bell. That means I'm chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And yet you stopped talking when I rang it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After I finish deciding whether you may.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats the bell as chairing authority, A3 cites its silencing effect, and A5 uses possession to reserve permission over its transfer.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's bicycle correction produces A3's functional authority argument; B4's borrowing request lets A5 exercise the claimed chair power.

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges the object's status and B4 offers a simple transfer test.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's borrowing request to retain decision control, though the escalation is deliberately small.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a meeting bell and B2 identifies its ordinary bicycle origin.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's permission-before-permission loop is concise and directly triggered by B4.
